title: Federated archives & multi-modal repositories
intro: Start here. These are the general-purpose, standards-based archives that hold data from many labs; for most modalities one of them is the canonical place to look before searching for a lab-specific portal.

title: Reference atlases & coordinate frameworks
intro: Reference spaces and anatomical frameworks. Registering your own data into one of these is usually the precondition for comparing it to anything else in this list.

title: Transcriptomics, epigenomics & spatial omics
intro: Gene- and cell-level molecular data: bulk, single-cell, single-nucleus, epigenomic and spatial.

title: Connectomics, projections & neuron morphology
intro: Wiring diagrams at every scale — synapse-level electron microscopy, mesoscale projection matrices, single-neuron morphology, and macroscale diffusion connectomes.

title: Neurophysiology & neural activity (animal)
intro: Recorded neural activity in animals: electrophysiology, calcium imaging, and the standardized behavioral tasks they were recorded during.

title: Human electrophysiology (EEG / MEG / iEEG)
intro: Non-invasive and intracranial human electrophysiology, including clinical corpora and brain-computer-interface benchmarks.

title: Human neuroimaging cohorts & population studies
intro: Human MRI and PET, from small frictionless method-development datasets to population cohorts of 100,000 participants.

title: Behavior, video & pose datasets
intro: Raw and annotated behavior video, pose-estimation ground truth, and strain-level phenotype compendia.

title: Computational models, simulation & benchmarks
intro: Model source code, simulation platforms, whole-brain simulators and benchmarks that score models against neural data.

title: Organoids, stem cells & in-vitro models
intro: In-vitro human neural models: organoid single-cell atlases, iPSC line registries, and microelectrode-array recordings.

title: Model-organism knowledgebases
intro: The per-species knowledgebases that connect genes and genetic reagents to nervous-system anatomy.

title: Disease, genetics & biobank portals
intro: Disease cohorts, genetic association resources and the post-mortem tissue banks behind most human molecular neuroscience.

title: Standards, tooling & resource catalogs
intro: The formats, metadata schemas and registries that make everything above interoperable — and the catalogs to use when this list runs out.
